A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CacheAttack research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original response-hijacking, agent-tool, transferability, defense and sensitivity experiments, plus a financial-agent case study.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds genetic-algorithm baseline results and evaluations on AWS Bedrock and Azure API Management.

M1.justification: The proposed GCG-based generator, collision and perplexity objectives, latency validator, and CacheAttack-1/2 procedures remain unchanged. The genetic algorithm is an added comparator, not a revision of CacheAttack.

E1.justification: v2 extends RQ1 beyond GPTCache and the SemShareKV reimplementation to AWS Bedrock and Azure API Management, substantially broadening the tested deployment environments (Table 2). NQ, SC-IPI, BFCL-derived tasks and the financial-agent scenario are retained.

E2.justification: v1 compares clean execution with the two CacheAttack variants. v2 adds a genetic-algorithm attack baseline to the existing response-hijacking comparison and the new service comparison, introducing the first alternative attack generator actually evaluated against CacheAttack.

E3.justification: The added GA comparison explicitly holds the validator fixed, and the new service evaluation reports HR alone rather than the HR/ISR pair used in the original RQ1 table. Existing sample sizes, 1000-step search budget, threshold and sensitivity settings remain unchanged; service-specific configurations are not detailed.

E4.justification: The transferability, backend-model sensitivity, threshold sweep, defense analyses and financial-agent case study are retained. New Appendix D redisplays the existing perplexity plot and backend-results table; it does not introduce another supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-estimate reporting without evaluation seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The latency-validator statistical model and discussion of variation across backend models are unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds GA HR/ISR results of 36.2/33.7% for semantic cache and 34.0/31.5% for semantic KV cache. New Table 2 reports AWS/Azure HRs of 80.6/88.3% for CacheAttack-1, 78.2/86.7% for CacheAttack-2 and 12.4/15.2% for GA. Previously reported results remain unchanged; these are additional comparisons, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: v1's locality-versus-collision argument is conceptual. v2 adds Lemma 3.1, defining the incorrect-reuse event B and bounding P(B | hit) below by 1 - P(not B)/h, together with a conditional-probability proof in new Appendix A. This introduces a formal result supporting a central argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same core claims about fuzzy hashing, the locality-security trade-off, CacheAttack, response/tool hijacking and transferability, including the 86% headline hit rate. The new theorem and experiments supply additional support.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, backend-insensitivity interpretation, financial-agent implications and defense trade-offs remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or failure-condition discussion is added. The new Impact Statement largely restates security relevance and reports responsible-disclosure coordination.

D1.justification: Section 6.1 newly specifies cosine-similarity fitness and reuse of the existing validator for the GA baseline. Existing embedding choices, threshold, suffix constraint, dataset-construction instructions and code link are retained. Detailed GA hyperparameters and cloud-service configurations are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lambora et al. (2019) and two concurrent cache-security studies by Wu et al. (2026a,b). Section 2.4 acknowledges their empirical poisoning findings and distinguishes this work through key-collision formalization and the locality-resistance argument; the broader related-work discussion is retained.

P1.justification: v2 lightly edits the abstract, updates publication text and heading capitalization, adds an Impact Statement, and reorganizes the appendices around the proof and an extra-results section. Most prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds a GA row to Table 1 and a separate service-results table. The perplexity chart moves from main-text Figure 3 to appendix Figure 4 and is enlarged; the retained backend table moves into Appendix D. Other displays mainly shift or receive new numbering.

improvement.justification: The GA comparison and cloud-service hit-rate measurements improve empirical context beyond v1's clean/own-variant comparisons and implementation-based evaluations. The proof and acknowledgment of concurrent research also improve support and positioning. These gains remain limited by sparse GA/service configuration details and unchanged uncertainty reporting; the elementary bound can be vacuous and does not independently establish the broad security claim.
